angles.angle: News consumption has shifted from scheduled broadcasts to constant, on-demand updates
angles.example: people now check news apps throughout the day rather than waiting for the evening bulletin

angles.angle: Social media accelerates the spread of news but also amplifies misinformation
angles.example: an unverified claim can go viral before fact-checkers have a chance to respond

angles.angle: Traditional news organisations carry a responsibility for accuracy that many social platforms don't enforce
angles.example: a newspaper retracts and corrects errors publicly, while a viral post rarely gets the same correction

angles.angle: Constant exposure to negative news can affect mental wellbeing, leading some to limit their intake
angles.example: the term 'doomscrolling' describes the habit of compulsively consuming distressing news

angles.angle: Algorithmic curation can trap people in narrow viewpoints, reducing exposure to balanced perspectives
angles.example: personalised feeds tend to show more of what a user already agrees with
